narrative.headline: ⚠️ THIS RECONSTRUCTION DOES NOT RECONCILE with Polymarket's own profit figure for the wallet, so the numbers below are wrong by an unknown amount — most likely it exits through an activity type the feed does not publish, such as a merge. Read the shape, not the totals. 0x5139cbd6 deployed $224,079 across 517 events in 52 days and finished $25,366 — a yield of +11.32% on money at risk. 93% of that capital went in after kick-off, the median position was held 2.3 h, and the median ticket was $109.99.

sections.title: What it does
paragraphs: **Archetype: Stale-order sweeper, Near-certainty grinder, Systematic / automated.**

— *Stale-order sweeper* (high confidence): 71 lots entered at ≤0.15 and exited at ≥3× carry MORE than all of the profit (126%) — the rest of the book loses money — on 0.2% of the capital; median sweep ticket $5.05, median hold 4.8 min, across 70 events.
— *Near-certainty grinder* (high confidence): 100% of capital enters above 0.90 — thin margins, high turnover; capital recycled 78.4× against a peak book of $2,860.
— *Systematic / automated* (high confidence): 2,488 fills across 517 events, 47 fills per active day; median ticket $109.99 — size is uniform, which is what a script looks like.
It trades 518 markets over 517 fixtures — 2,488 fills, 47 per active day over 53 days with activity. It buys at an average of 0.870 and sells at 0.989.
Where it plays: ITF (64% of capital, +12%), ATP Tour (28% of capital, +5%), WTA Tour (9% of capital, +11%), MLB (0% of capital, +9634%).
Market types: tennis_completed_match 100%, baseball_player_hits_runs_rbis 0%, second_half_spreads 0%, totals 0%.

sections.title: Where the money comes from
paragraphs: **The money is made after settlement time**: $62,213 deployed there returned $14,799 (+23.8%), which is 58% of all profit on 28% of the capital.

In-play, the modal trade goes nowhere: the flat -0.05..+0.02 bucket is 1,217 lots and $125,792 of capital for $76.96. The > +0.30 bucket is 10 lots and $4,421. The tail pays for the bleed — any copy of this has to be sized for that, because most positions lose the spread.
Exits: 19% sold back into the book, 80% redeemed at settlement, 0% simply left to resolve ($0.00 of that expired worthless).

sections.title: How it evolved
paragraphs: Across 2 complete months the book grew from $22,006 to $133,539 of monthly turnover, and the yield is **improving** — +4.1% over the first 1 month(s) against +18.2% over the last 1. Yield rising while turnover holds or grows is the signature of a repeatable process rather than a lucky run.
2026-10 is still in progress ($68,534 deployed, +0.3%) and is excluded from the trend.
**Regime change in 2026-09**: the share of capital committed before kick-off moved 58% → 2%. That is a different strategy, not a different month — split any evaluation there.

Day to day it wins 49 of 53 sessions — best $3,757, worst -$794.38, longest losing streak 1 days. Peak open book $2,860; the cumulative cash floor is -$930.14, so it had to carry a real bankroll, not just recycle winnings.

sections.title: Is the edge real?
paragraphs: Bootstrapped over 517 events (resampled by event, not by lot, because lots inside one fixture are the same bet taken repeatedly): yield +11.32%, 95% CI [+6.57%, +16.68%], p(≤0) = 0.0000. The interval clears zero — the edge in this wallet's own record is real.

Concentration: top event 6% of profit, top 5 27%, top 10 50%; 86% of events profitable. Drop the 200 best individual lots and the rest of the book LOSES $6,751 (-3.01%) — the entire result is those 200 trades. The result does not depend on a handful of bets.

Reconciliation: Polymarket's own all-time profit for this wallet is $26,157, counted before fees; on the same basis (P&L plus $2,240 of fees paid) our reconstruction brackets it at $27,606 … $28,666 (**it falls outside — do not trust these numbers**; something in the reconstruction is wrong, most likely an activity type we do not model).

sections.title: What is not established
paragraphs: ⚠️ 6 lots sold shares that never appear as a purchase ($1,060 of proceeds) — neg-risk conversions, which Polymarket's activity feed does not publish. They are booked FLAT, so they add no profit; the true figure is inside the bracket above, not at either end.

⚠️ Only 0% of this wallet's capital is in competitions we recognise as football (0% is unrecognised). The 110-130' whistle window is a football fact and means nothing on the rest — read the timing table for football wallets only.

⚠️ Selection bias on the wallet itself. You are reading it because someone pointed at it. The statistics describe the edge in its own record; they cannot tell you how many identically-shaped wallets blew up unseen.
⚠️ `lb-api` 'volume' is SHARES, not dollars, and its windowed figures do not reconcile. Only `window=all` is used here.
